points: Bristol-Myers Squibb Company does business as Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS).
BMS is an American multinational pharmaceutical company.
BMS is headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey.
Apixaban, sold as Eliquis, is a primary BMS product.
Apixaban is used for people with atrial fibrillation.
Apixaban accounted for 30% of BMS's 2025 revenue.
Nivolumab, sold as Opdivo, is a primary BMS product.
Nivolumab is used to treat certain cancers.
Nivolumab accounted for 21% of BMS's 2025 revenue.
Lenalidomide, sold as Revlimid, is a primary BMS product.
Lenalidomide treats multiple myeloma.
Lenalidomide treats smoldering myeloma.
Lenalidomide treats myelodysplastic syndromes.
Lenalidomide accounted for 6% of BMS's 2025 revenue.
Abatacept, sold as Orencia, is a primary BMS product.
Abatacept treats autoimmune diseases.
Rheumatoid arthritis is an example of an autoimmune disease treated with abatacept.
Abatacept accounted for 8% of BMS's 2025 revenue.
Pomalidomide, sold as Pomalyst or Imnovid, is a primary BMS product.
Pomalidomide is an anticancer drug.
Pomalidomide treats multiple myeloma.
Pomalidomide treats AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma.
Pomalidomide accounted for 6% of BMS's 2025 revenue.
Ipilimumab, sold as Yervoy, is a primary BMS product.
Ipilimumab treats cancer.
Ipilimumab accounted for 6% of BMS's 2025 revenue.
Luspatercept, sold as Reblozyl, is a primary BMS product.
Luspatercept treats anemia associated with beta thalassemia.
Luspatercept treats anemia associated with myelodysplastic syndromes.
Luspatercept accounted for 5% of BMS's 2025 revenue.
The United States accounted for 69% of BMS's 2025 revenue.
BMS ranks 94th on the Fortune 500.
BMS ranks 173rd on the Forbes Global 2000.
BMS has a primary research and development site in Lawrence, New Jersey.
The Lawrence site was formerly a Squibb site.
Lawrence is near Princeton.
BMS has a primary research and development site in Summit, New Jersey.
The Summit site formerly housed Celgene's headquarters.
BMS has a primary research and development site in New Brunswick, New Jersey.
BMS has a primary research and development site in Redwood City, California.
BMS has a primary research and development site in Seville, Spain.
BMS has a research and development site in Devens, Massachusetts.
BMS has a research and development site in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
BMS has a research and development site in Braine-l'Alleud, Belgium.
BMS has a research and development site in Tokyo, Japan.
BMS has a research and development site in Hyderabad, India.
BMS has a research and development site in Bangalore, India.
BMS has a research and development site in Wirral, United Kingdom.
BMS formerly had a research and development site in Wallingford, Connecticut.
The Wallingford site originally belonged to Bristol-Myers.
Edward Robinson Squibb founded the Squibb corporation in 1858.
Squibb was founded in Brooklyn, New York.
Edward Robinson Squibb resigned from his post as a U.S. Navy assistant surgeon before founding the company.
Squibb began operating in a small brick laboratory in Brooklyn.
Squibb's first laboratory burned down on Christmas Eve 1858.
The fire reportedly nearly put the newly opened company out of business.
Doctors and surgeons subscribed $2,100 to help Squibb reopen.
Squibb reopened in 1859.
Squibb survived the fire and went on to flourish.
Edward Squibb was an early advocate of pharmaceutical quality control.
Edward Squibb advocated high pharmaceutical purity standards.
The American Medical Association did not adopt the higher purity standards that Edward Squibb urged it to incorporate.
After failing to persuade the association, Edward Squibb self-published Squibb's Ephemeris of Materia Medica as an alternative to the U.S. Pharmacopeia.
Squibb's Materia Medica appeared in many late-19th-century medical papers.
Squibb products appeared in many late-19th-century medical papers.
Edward Squibb's views on the fundamentals of pharmacy appeared in many late-19th-century medical papers.
The American Journal of Pharmacy published more than 100 papers on Edward Squibb's pharmaceutical research.
Edward Squibb's declining health led him to pass management to his sons, Charles and Edward.
By 1895, the company was officially named E.R. Squibb & Sons.
Edward Squibb's sons sold the company to Lowell M. Palmer and Theodore Weicker in 1905.
Palmer and Weicker incorporated the company.
The Squibb logo was developed around the time of the 1905 sale and incorporation.
The Squibb logo represented uniformity, purity, efficacy, and reliability based on research.
Squibb was a major supplier of medical goods to the Union Army during the American Civil War.
Squibb supplied the Union Army with portable medical kits.
The medical kits contained morphine.
The medical kits contained surgical anesthetics.
The medical kits contained quinine to treat malaria.
Malaria was endemic in most of the eastern United States during the Civil War.
Squibb opened what was then the world's largest penicillin plant in 1944.
Squibb's record-size penicillin plant was in New Brunswick, New Jersey.
William McLaren Bristol and John Ripley Myers bought the Clinton Pharmaceutical Company in 1887.
William McLaren Bristol was a Hamilton College graduate.
John Ripley Myers was a Hamilton College graduate.
The Clinton Pharmaceutical Company was based in Clinton, New York.
Bristol and Myers decided to rename the company Bristol, Myers and Company in May 1898.
John Ripley Myers died in 1899.
After Myers died, Bristol renamed the company the Bristol-Myers Corporation.
The company introduced Sal Hepatica, its first nationally recognized product, in the 1890s.
Sal Hepatica was a laxative mineral salt.
The company introduced Ipana toothpaste in 1901.
Clairol was a Bristol-Myers division.
Clairol sold hair-color and hair-care products.
Drackett was a Bristol-Myers division.
Drackett sold household products.
Windex was a Drackett product.
Drano was a Drackett product.
Bristol-Myers acquired Cheplin Biological Laboratories in 1943.
Cheplin Biological Laboratories produced acidophilus milk.
Cheplin's plant was in East Syracuse, New York.
Bristol-Myers converted the East Syracuse plant to make penicillin for the Allied forces during World War II.
Bristol-Myers renamed the East Syracuse plant Bristol Laboratories in 1945.
Bristol-Myers entered the civilian antibiotics market after World War II.
Bristol-Myers competed with Squibb in the civilian antibiotics market.
The East Syracuse plant stopped making penicillin in 2005.
Penicillin production ended at East Syracuse because it became cheaper to make overseas.
As of 2010, the East Syracuse facility was used to develop manufacturing processes for other biologic medicines.
As of 2010, the East Syracuse facility produced other biologic medicines for clinical trials.
As of 2010, the East Syracuse facility produced other biologic medicines for commercial use.
Bristol-Myers and Squibb merged in 1989 to form Bristol-Myers Squibb.
U.S. President Bill Clinton awarded BMS the National Medal of Technology in 1999.
The National Medal of Technology was described as the highest U.S. recognition for technological achievement.
The award recognized BMS for extending and improving human life through innovative pharmaceutical research and development.
The award recognized BMS for advancing clinical research through pioneering, highly complex trials that became models for the industry.
The FBI raided BMS's corporate offices in July 2006 over allegations of collusion in the distribution of Plavix.
Frederick B. Lacey, the company monitor, was a former federal judge.
On September 12, 2006, Lacey urged BMS to remove CEO Peter Dolan over the Plavix dispute.
BMS announced later that day that Dolan would step down.
BMS's deferred prosecution agreement expired in June 2007.
The U.S. Department of Justice took no further legal action against BMS on matters covered by the deferred prosecution agreement.
Jim Cornelius succeeded Peter Dolan as CEO.
Jim Cornelius remained CEO until May 2010.
All executives implicated in the channel-stuffing and generic competition scandals left BMS under Jim Cornelius.
BMS launched a strategy in 2007 to transform itself from a large, diversified pharmaceutical company into a specialty biopharmaceutical company.
In 2009, BMS began a major restructuring focused on its pharmaceutical business and biologic products.
The restructuring included initiatives to improve productivity.
BMS used a multiyear program of layoffs to cut costs and streamline operations.
The transformation strategy included closing half of BMS's manufacturing facilities.
BMS reduced retiree health-care subsidies to cut costs.
BMS planned to freeze its retiree pension plan at the end of 2009.
Lamberto Andreotti was named CEO of BMS in 2010.
Andreotti had previously served as BMS president.
Andreotti had previously served as BMS chief operating officer.
Lou Schmukler joined BMS in 2010 as president of global product development and design.
Schmukler led the team that completed BMS's transformation into a specialty biopharmaceutical company.
BMS had 12 manufacturing facilities as of 2011.
BMS had six product development sites as of 2011.
Forbes ranked BMS the best drug company of 2013.
Nivolumab is a PD-1 inhibitor.
In December 2014, the FDA approved nivolumab for patients whose skin cancer could not be removed.
The December 2014 approval also covered skin cancer patients who had not responded to prior drug treatments.
BMS began a research partnership with Rigel Pharmaceuticals in February 2015.
The Rigel partnership could generate more than $339 million.
In March 2015, BMS obtained an exclusive opportunity to license PROSTVAC from Bavarian Nordic.
BMS also obtained an exclusive opportunity to commercialize PROSTVAC.
PROSTVAC was a Phase III cancer immunotherapy.
PROSTVAC targeted prostate-specific antigen.
The PROSTVAC deal provided for a $60 million upfront payment to Bavarian Nordic.
Bavarian Nordic could receive up to $230 million in additional payments if overall patient survival exceeded what was observed in Phase II.
Bavarian Nordic could receive regulatory milestones of $110 million to $495 million, depending on authorization.
Potential payments under the PROSTVAC deal could total up to $975 million.
Giovanni Caforio became CEO of BMS in May 2015.
Caforio had previously been BMS's chief operating officer.
Caforio succeeded Lamberto Andreotti upon Andreotti's retirement as CEO.
Andreotti later succeeded James Cornelius as executive chairman when Cornelius retired.
BMS acquired the biotechnology firm Medarex in August 2009 during its restructuring.
The Medarex purchase was part of BMS's String of Pearls strategy of alliances, partnerships, and acquisitions.
BMS announced a split-off of Mead Johnson Nutrition in November 2009.
The split-off offered BMS shareholders the chance to exchange their stock for Mead Johnson shares.
BMS expected the Mead Johnson split-off to sharpen its focus on biopharmaceuticals.
BMS acquired ZymoGenetics in October 2010.
The ZymoGenetics purchase gave BMS an existing product.
The ZymoGenetics purchase added hepatitis C pipeline assets.
The ZymoGenetics purchase added cancer pipeline assets.
The ZymoGenetics purchase added pipeline assets in other therapeutic areas.
BMS agreed to buy Inhibitex for about $2.5 billion in cash.
BMS pursued Inhibitex to compete with Gilead and Pharmasset in hepatitis C drugs.
The Inhibitex deal was expected to close in two months, subject to acceptance by Inhibitex shareholders.
The Inhibitex bid represented a 126% premium over the price benchmark for the 20 trading days ending January 6.
On June 29, BMS agreed to buy Amylin Pharmaceuticals for about $5.3 billion in cash.
The Amylin deal expanded BMS's portfolio of diabetes treatments.
BMS agreed to pay Eli Lilly $1.7 billion to cover Amylin's debt and outstanding collaboration obligations.
AstraZeneca was already working with BMS on several diabetes treatments.
AstraZeneca agreed to pay $3.4 billion in cash for the right to continue developing Amylin's products.
BMS divested Amylin to AstraZeneca two years after agreeing to buy it.
BMS announced the acquisition of iPierian in April 2014.
The iPierian deal was valued at up to $725 million.
BMS acquired Flexus Biosciences in February 2015.
The Flexus acquisition was valued at $1.25 billion.
The Flexus deal gave BMS full rights to F001287.
F001287 was Flexus's lead small-molecule IDO1 inhibitor.
BMS acquired Cardioxyl in November 2015.
Cardioxyl developed drugs for cardiovascular disease.
The Cardioxyl deal was valued at up to $2.075 billion.
The Cardioxyl deal strengthened BMS's pipeline by adding CXL-1427.
CXL-1427 was a Phase II candidate for acute decompensated heart failure.
BMS announced plans to acquire Padlock Therapeutics in March 2016.
The Padlock deal was valued at up to $600 million.
BMS announced plans to acquire Cormorant Pharmaceuticals in early July 2016.
The Cormorant deal was valued at $520 million.
The Cormorant deal expanded BMS's cancer-drug portfolio.
Cormorant brought a monoclonal antibody targeting interleukin-8.
BMS acquired IFM Therapeutics in August 2017.
BMS agreed to pay $300 million upfront for IFM Therapeutics.
The IFM deal provided for $1.01 billion in payments tied to milestones.
The IFM deal helped BMS compete with Keytruda, Merck & Co.'s cancer treatment.
BMS acquired Celgene in November 2019.
The Celgene acquisition cost $74 billion.
The Celgene acquisition was valued at $95 billion including debt.
Amgen bought Otezla from Celgene to allow the BMS-Celgene deal to receive regulatory approval.
Amgen paid $13.4 billion for Otezla.
BMS intended the Celgene acquisition to refresh its drug pipeline.
The Celgene acquisition was meant to help BMS respond to Opdivo's declining sales relative to Keytruda.
BMS investor Wellington Management Company opposed the Celgene merger.
BMS investor Starboard Value opposed the Celgene merger.
Seventy-five percent of BMS shareholders voted to approve the Celgene merger.
BMS sold its consumer health business, UPSA, to Taisho Pharmaceutical in July 2019.
UPSA focused on delivering products in France and the rest of Europe.
BMS had divested individual consumer products as early as 2005.
BMS had divested its U.S.- and Canada-focused consumer products business as early as 2005.
BMS and its partner Biomotiv launched Anteros Pharmaceuticals in February 2020.
Anteros focuses on developing medicines for inflammation.
Anteros focuses on developing medicines for fibrosis.
BMS announced plans to acquire Forbius in August 2020.
The Forbius deal included inhibitors of TGF-beta 1 and TGF-beta 3.
BMS announced plans to acquire the cardiology company MyoKardia in October 2020.
The MyoKardia deal was valued at $13.1 billion.
The MyoKardia deal was priced at $225 per share.
The MyoKardia deal gave BMS control of mavacamten.
Mavacamten is a cardiovascular drug for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
The MyoKardia deal gave BMS control of development of danicamtiv, also known as MYK-491.
The MyoKardia deal gave BMS control of development of MYK-224.
BMS acquired Turning Point Therapeutics in August 2022.
BMS paid $4.1 billion in cash for Turning Point Therapeutics.
The Turning Point deal expanded BMS's cancer-drug portfolio, notably by adding repotrectinib.
In August 2022, BMS announced a $180 million investment in Owkin.
Owkin is a French artificial intelligence company.
The Owkin collaboration aimed to design potentially more precise clinical trials.
The Owkin collaboration aimed to design potentially more efficient clinical trials.
The Owkin collaboration was to focus initially on cardiovascular disease.
The Owkin collaboration could expand to other therapeutic areas.
BMS partnered with Cellares in August 2023 to produce CAR-T treatments using robotics.
BMS had two approved CAR-T treatments at the time of the Cellares partnership.
In September 2023, BMS announced a strategic licensing and collaboration deal with Zenas BioPharma to develop obexelimab.
The Zenas deal also covered commercialization of obexelimab.
BMS agreed to pay Zenas BioPharma $50 million upfront.
Obexelimab is a novel bifunctional antibody for autoimmune diseases.
BMS acquired Mirati Therapeutics in January 2024.
Mirati Therapeutics is an American biotechnology company.
Mirati develops targeted cancer treatments.
The Mirati acquisition was priced at $4.8 billion.
The Mirati deal included an additional $1 billion milestone payment.
BMS acquired Karuna Therapeutics in March 2024.
BMS paid $14 billion for Karuna Therapeutics.
The deal included Karuna's lead drug candidate, KarXT.
KarXT was an investigational muscarinic antipsychotic.
KarXT combined xanomeline and trospium.
KarXT was intended to treat schizophrenia in adults.
BMS acquired RayzeBio in February 2024.
The RayzeBio deal was valued at approximately $4.1 billion.
The FDA approved Cobenfy in September 2024.
Cobenfy was the first new type of schizophrenia treatment in 70 years.
Sal Hepatica is out of production.
Ipana is out of production.
Bristol-Myers divested Bufferin.
Bristol-Myers divested Excedrin.
Bristol-Myers divested Ban Deodorant.
Bristol-Myers divested Vitalis.
Vitalis is a hair tonic.
Bristol-Myers divested Ammens.
Ammens is a medicated powder.
Bristol-Myers divested Final Net.
Final Net is a hair spray.
Bristol-Myers divested Comtrex.
Comtrex is a cold relief capsule product.
Bristol-Myers divested Keri.
Keri is a lotion.
The article's 2023 list of products under development is selective, not exhaustive.
Luspatercept was listed in Phase III.
The FDA expanded the Reblozyl label on August 28, 2023.
The label expansion made Reblozyl a first-line treatment option for anemia in adults with low- to intermediate-risk myelodysplastic syndromes who may need regular blood transfusions.
Data from the Phase III COMMANDS study supported the Reblozyl label expansion.
Reblozyl outperformed erythropoiesis-stimulating agents in treating anemia related to myelodysplastic syndromes.
The label expansion could help Reblozyl reach its $4 billion sales goal by 2030.
Reblozyl was effective in patients with the symptoms referenced in the article.
Reblozyl was also effective in patients without those symptoms, broadening its potential use.

BMS-955176 was listed in Phase II.

Elotuzumab, also known as BMS-901608, was listed in Phase III.

Lulizumab pegol, also known as BMS-931699, was listed in Phase II.

BMS contributed to the lobbying organization National Health Council.
BMS contributed to the lobbying organization Pharmaceutical Advertising Advisory Board.
BMS contributed to the lobbying organization Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America.
In 2002, 29 states sued BMS over allegations that it illegally maintained a monopoly on Taxol.
Taxol is a cancer treatment.
In a separate 2002 case, BMS was sued for allegedly trying to keep a generic version of BuSpar off the market.
BMS paid $125 million to settle the Taxol case.
BMS paid a total of $670 million to settle the Taxol and BuSpar cases.
BMS was involved in an accounting scandal in 2002.
The accounting scandal led to a significant restatement of revenue for 1999 through 2001.
Improper recording of sales tied to channel stuffing caused the revenue restatement.
Channel stuffing involves offering customers excess inventory to inflate reported sales.
BMS paid $150 million to settle with the U.S. Department of Justice and the Securities and Exchange Commission.
In 2004, BMS restated its financial results for the previous five years.
A deferred prosecution agreement put BMS under a monitor's oversight.
The U.S. attorney in New Jersey appointed the monitor.
Richard Lane, the former head of BMS's Pharma group, was indicted for federal securities violations.
Fred Schiff, BMS's former chief financial officer, was indicted for federal securities violations.
BMS was named as a defendant in a $1 billion lawsuit over the Guatemala syphilis experiments.
The lawsuit concerned the infection of hundreds of Guatemalans with syphilis during the experiments.
BMS was dismissed from the Guatemala lawsuit in 2022.
The reason BMS was dismissed from the Guatemala lawsuit was not publicly disclosed.
